# sdd: start t1 --risk low --proposal docs/proposal.md
# sdd: advance proposed
# sdd: advance red
# sdd: advance red --test-cmd true
# sdd: advance red --test-cmd 'test -f fixed'
# sdd: advance green --test-cmd true
# sdd: advance green
# sh: touch fixed
# sdd: advance green
# sdd: status
$ sdd start t1 --risk low --proposal docs/proposal.md
task 't1' opened (risk=low, profile=standard, phase=intake). Write the proposal with a Definition of Done, then: sdkit sdd advance proposed
exit: 0
$ sdd advance proposed
phase: proposed
exit: 0
$ sdd advance red
sdd: --test-cmd is required: the command that runs the new tests
exit: 1
$ sdd advance red --test-cmd true
sdd: the tests PASS, so they prove nothing yet. They must fail for the right reason first (see .sdkit/.sdd/last-test.log).
exit: 1
$ sdd advance red --test-cmd 'test -f fixed'
phase: red
exit: 0
$ sdd advance green --test-cmd true
sdd: GREEN re-runs the command that failed at RED ('test -f fixed'); a different command proves nothing about those tests. Run 'sdkit sdd advance green' without --test-cmd.
exit: 1
$ sdd advance green
sdd: the tests still fail (full output: .sdkit/.sdd/last-test.log)
exit: 1
$ sdd advance green
phase: green
exit: 0
$ sdd status
task=t1 risk=low phase=green
exit: 0
